changes: Scope contracts now persist one versioned repo-root path identity, TypeScript semantic scope uses parser-backed current/previous declaration anchors across edits, deletions and renames, and official B-META gap_log metadata is accepted only through a tamper-evident append ledger shared by scope, prewrite, guard-session and done_prepare consumers.
usage: Use scope_contract_set/init_from_plan normally; source-root inputs such as core/foo.ts canonicalize to packages/main/src/core/foo.ts. Semantic gates automatically bind declaration identities, and gap_log remains the only supported writer for trusted B-META framework findings.
expectedOutcome: The terminal prints: input: core/foo.ts | canonical: packages/main/src/core/foo.ts | rule: allowed_modify | status: PASS, while semantic-anchor and B-META provenance smoke checks also pass.
actualTranscript: Live smoke exited 0 and printed the exact canonical path PASS line, followed by semantic scope guard smoke passed and gap-log full provenance, consumer parity, legacy genesis, and diagnostic matrix PASS.
outcomeDiff: No user-visible difference: actual output matched the expected canonical path line and both additional safety checks passed.
limitations: The B-META ledger provides cooperative local tamper evidence and canonical-command causal lineage; without an external secret or OS trust boundary it does not claim authentication against a same-UID actor that can rewrite Git history.
pitfalls: Five targeted review rounds exposed partial coverage and adjacent rename/deletion/glob/provenance cases; the final matrix covers them explicitly. The first TEST transition left an active validate child after its parent channel exited, and one 0-command reuse attempt saw pre-existing Lattice metadata dirt; the existing process was monitored, generated metadata was persisted, and the next clean-entry reuse converged without re-running commands.
